m.d: all or every one in a group separately
m.e: Come here you two. I'll give each of you a toy.

m.d: If you eat something, usually food, you put it in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it.
m.e: I always eat too much good when it's Thanksgiving.

m.d: If you eat the cost of something, you pay for it.
m.e: The supplier will have to eat the cost of returning the goods.

m.d: If you eat someone, you give them sex with your mouth (oral sex)
If something is easy, it does not need much skill or effort.
m.e: The teacher gave an easy test to her students.

m.d: If you do something easy, you do slowly, without effort, calmly.
m.e: Take it easy. (See also take it easy.)

m.d: Some soil.
m.e: I planted some roses in this patch of earth.

m.d: Anything made up mostly of rock, sand or soil.
m.e: Here is some earth.

m.d: Earth is the third planet from the sun, where we live.
m.e: The Earth is a planet.

m.d: If something is early, it is sooner than expected.
m.e: It was an early end to the meeting.

m.d: If something is early, it happens in the first part of a time period.
m.e: He didn't like going to the early classes.

m.d: Sooner than expected.
m.e: He was at the meeting early.

m.d: During the first part of a time period.
m.e: She got up early in the morning.

m.d: before
m.e: She had left three days earlier.

m.d: The east is a place that is closer to where the sun rises than another place.
m.e: My parents live in the east.

m.d: East is a surname.
One of the four compass directions: 90º clockwise from north. The sun rises in the east.
m.e: I drove east from Chicago.

m.d: If you do something easily, you have no trouble doing it.
m.e: They won the game easily, 6–0.

m.d: If something could easily happen, it is likely.
A part of the head (or face) used for hearing.
m.e: My rabbit has two big ears.

m.d: If you earn something you get it by working or doing something.
m.e: I earn a lot more money at my new job than at my last job.

m.d: If you think you have earned something, you think you should have it because of what you have done.
m.e: After completing that project I thought I had earned some time to rest.

m.d: The state of being comfortable or relaxed.
m.e: She enjoyed the ease of living in a house where the servants did all the work.

m.d: Free from pain, worry, etc.
m.e: His mind was at ease when he took the test. He knew he had studied well.

m.d: Free from effort, difficulty or hardship.
m.e: He passed all the exams with ease.

m.d: To free or lessen (something) from pain, worry, agitation, etc.
m.e: He eased his conscience telling her what he had done wrong.

m.d: To loosen or relax the tension on (something).
m.e: We eased the rope, then lowered the sail.

m.d: To reduce the difficulty of (something).
m.e: We had to ease the entry requirements.

m.d: An earl is a British or Irish nobleman next in rank above a viscount and below a marquess; equivalent to a European count.
Earl is a surname.
Earl is a male given name.
A type of meat-eating bird.
m.e: He saw an eagle perched on top of that tree.

m.d: An old gold coin in the United States worth $10.
m.e: He showed me his coin collection. He even had an old eagle.

m.d: A score of two under par for a hole.
m.e: I got a birdy and you got an eagle on that last hole.

m.d: If you eagle a golf hole, you score two under par on it.
m.e: I eagled the last hole with 3 strokes on a par 5.

m.d: Food.
m.e: Give me some eats!

m.d: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the east.
m.e: Washington, D.C. is on the eastern side of United States.

m.d: Blowing from the east; easterly.
Asia.
To be eager is to hardly be able to wait to do something.
m.e: They were eager to see the new movie.

m.d: An earthquake is a natural event that causes the ground to shake up and down, and sometimes, may destroy buildings.
m.e: The earthquake ripped a crack in the road and destroyed half of the building that I live in.

m.d: Easter is a Christian celebration, usually in April, of the day when Christians believe that Jesus of Nazareth came back from the dead.
m.e: Our church will start Easter Sunday with a sunrise service at 6 a.m.

m.d: An earring is a piece of jewelry worn on the ear.
m.e: She wore golden earrings.

m.d: If something is earthly, it is related to the Earth.
An eater eats something. An eater of x, eats mostly x.
m.e: She's not a meat eater.

m.d: Your earnings is the amount of money you obtain from doing something.
m.e: All my earnings for the year wouldn't cover the cost of one of her designer dresses.

m.d: If someone is earnest, they are serious and truly believe in what they say or do.
If something is done eagerly, it is done in an eager manner.
Eastwood is a surname.
If you eavesdrop on a conversation, you secretly listen to it without anyone knowing.
m.e: I hope nobody was eavesdropping on our conversation last night, since it got so personal.
